hook.line: Where you live and what you eat are the first two things anyone in Bogotá asks a newcomer. Both verbs end in -er or -ir, and the good news is they work almost exactly like the -ar verbs you already have.
hook.es: Vivo en La Candelaria y como en el café de Rosa.
hook.en: I live in La Candelaria and I eat at Rosa's café.

examples.en: Do you live in Bogotá? (to a friend)

examples.es: Los clientes comen pan con el tinto.
examples.en: The customers eat bread with their coffee.
You all live in the neighbourhood, right?

rule:
Comer (to eat) and vivir (to live) take the same idea as trabajar: drop the ending, add who.

como / vivo: I eat, I live
comes / vives: you eat, you live (a friend)
come / vive: he, she eats or lives; you (usted)
comemos / vivimos: we eat, we live
comen / viven: they eat or live; you all

Spot the trick: where -ar verbs have an a (trabajas, trabaja), these have an e (comes, come). -er and -ir verbs are identical except in the we-form: comemos, but vivimos.

Creer (to believe) goes like comer: creo, crees, cree. And verbs you met as fixed phrases join in for everyone except I: Vale sabe, hace, ve; ¿sabes?, ¿haces?
smallPrint: This is the present tense (presente) of regular -er and -ir verbs.
soundTip: Stress the same syllable in every form except we: VI-vo, VI-ves, VI-ven, but vi-VI-mos. Same with CO-mo, CO-men, co-ME-mos.

options: I eat at two with Vale.
Vale and I eat at two.
You all eat in the park.

yourTurn.why: He or she = -e for both -er and -ir verbs.

yourTurn.prompt: Do you eat bread? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: You (a friend) = -es. The question marks do the asking.

yourTurn.prompt: The customers eat in the café.
yourTurn.answer: Los clientes comen en el café.

yourTurn.why: No goes right before the verb.
Saber is regular for everyone but I: sabe like come.

pitfalls.why: Vivir is an -ir verb, so we is vivimos. Only -er verbs say -emos: comemos.
Vivo means I live. For Vale (she), the ending is -e: vive.
After -ar verbs it's tempting to write an a, but -er verbs take e: comes, come, comen.

personal: Where do you live, and where do you usually eat? Write two short sentences with vivo and como.
